Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Please prepare a practical Monday-to-Friday watering rota for the Alder Lane learning greenhouse, using the reference notes below. Show who is responsible, the relevant zone, and the suggested time for each task. Account for the stated access arrangements and watering conditions, and make any conditional steps clear. If the notes do not settle a detail needed for the rota, flag it rather than assuming an answer. Keep the rota usable by the volunteers who open the greenhouse.

Reference notes

Alder Lane’s learning greenhouse is a long, narrow structure behind the community center, with its entrance on the south side and a water tap just inside the door. The spring rota covers the second full week of April, when the children’s gardening group meets on Wednesday afternoon and the volunteer team usually works from 8:00 to 10:00 on weekdays. The greenhouse is open to volunteers from 7:30 each morning; the caretaker locks the entrance at 5:30 p.m. No volunteer has a key to the outside hose store, so the rota should rely on the indoor tap and the two blue watering cans already kept beside it. A small hose is available for the central bed, but it must be drained and hung on its hook after use.

The growing areas are divided into four named zones. West Bench holds seed trays and recently pricked-out lettuce and calendula seedlings. The Central Bed contains six tomato plants and a short row of young cucumbers. East Bench is used for herbs, including mature rosemary, mint in separate pots, and newly sown coriander. The Propagation Shelf is a warm, shaded rack with cuttings and two covered trays; its cover is opened during the day and replaced before the greenhouse is locked. Three citrus tubs sit on the floor beside the east wall and are not included in the bench labels. A laminated map showing the four zones and the citrus tubs is clipped to the greenhouse door.

Watering needs differ across the space. The West Bench trays dry faster than the larger pots, but the seedlings should be checked before water is added because the lower trays can remain damp after a cloudy day. The tomato and cucumber bed is watered at soil level, not over the leaves. The rosemary prefers a lighter check than the mint, whose pots are allowed to drain fully into saucers that are emptied after watering. Coriander was sown on Friday and should be kept evenly moist while it germinates. The covered propagation trays are checked each morning for condensation; if the compost is moist and droplets are visible on the inside of the lids, they do not need extra water that day.

Mara Venn coordinates the weekday rota and normally arrives shortly before 8:00. Ivo Park is available Monday, Wednesday, and Friday mornings, while Linh Adebayo can come Tuesday and Thursday before 9:00. Jo Bell leads the children’s group on Wednesday and can supervise a short greenhouse check after 3:15 p.m., but cannot open the building in the morning. Tomas Reed can help on Monday and Thursday and is the only person on the team who has used the small hose; he has asked to be paired with someone for any hose task. Mara said, “If I’m checking the seedlings, I can also note which trays were already damp.” Linh replied, “Please leave the mint saucers empty when you finish; standing water brings fungus gnats.”

The caretaker’s wall thermometer is read at the start of the day and records the overnight minimum as well as the current temperature. The forecast for this week is changeable: Monday is expected to be bright, Tuesday may stay overcast, Wednesday is forecast to be cool, and showers are possible on Thursday. No reliable forecast is posted for Friday. Mara has asked volunteers to use the thermometer and the visible condition of the compost rather than treating the forecast as a watering instruction. If the overnight minimum is below 8°C, delay watering the Central Bed until the greenhouse has warmed, then check the soil again; do not water it early simply to keep to a clock time. This condition applies later in the week too, not just on the morning it is first mentioned.

1. On Monday, Tomas checked the hose connection and found no leak. He watered the central bed at soil level while Mara watched, drained the hose, and returned it to its hook. The West Bench trays were inspected, and two small lettuce trays were watered while the remaining trays were left alone because their compost was still damp. Mara recorded that the trays nearest the door dried first after a sunny weekend. The Propagation Shelf lids had light condensation, so no water was added there. The citrus tubs were checked by lifting the pots slightly; one felt lighter than the others, but the notes do not say whether it was watered.
2. On Tuesday, Linh arrived at 8:10 and found the greenhouse cool and cloudy. She checked the rosemary and mint pots separately, watered the mint, and emptied the saucers before leaving. She wrote that the rosemary compost was still cool and damp. The coriander surface had begun to dry in one corner, so Linh used a small amount of water over that patch. The propagation lids had no visible droplets, and the compost below them felt moist. She left a note asking the next volunteer to check the citrus tubs individually rather than giving all three the same amount.
3. On Wednesday, Ivo is expected before the children’s group, and Jo can make the later supervised check after 3:15. The group will look at the tomato flowers but is not scheduled to water the plants. Jo has a small jug for demonstrations and can return it to the shelf after use. If the group notices a dry seed tray, Jo should write its position on the door clipboard rather than reaching over the benches while supervising children. The group’s usual visit lasts about forty minutes, and the greenhouse must still be locked by the caretaker at the normal evening time.

On Thursday, the volunteer team plans to inspect the central bed, East Bench, and citrus tubs in addition to any trays that need attention. Showers may reduce the need to water, but rain does not reach the greenhouse interior. Tomas is available to assist with the hose if a bed watering is actually needed, and Linh is not available that day. The Propagation Shelf should still be checked for condensation and its covers returned before the building closes. Ivo has written on the clipboard, “The coriander is coming up unevenly; check the dry corner, but don’t soak the whole tray.” The note refers to the same coriander sowing on East Bench.

Friday is the final weekday in this rota period. Mara wants a brief handover note left on the clipboard for the following week, recording which zones were checked, what was watered, and any pots or trays that still need attention. The team has not decided who will take responsibility for watering on the following Monday, so the rota should not assign that task. The citrus tubs remain separate from the four labeled growing zones, and volunteers should record each tub’s condition separately if they check them. Before leaving on Friday, the last person should confirm that the indoor tap is fully off, the blue cans are beside it, the hose is drained and hung if it was used, and the propagation covers are back in place.", "output": "Request
